newsitem.title: CANADA: Barrick Gold capex/earnings to rise in '97.
newsitem.headline: Barrick Gold capex/earnings to rise in '97.

text.p: Barrick Gold Corp said on Thursday that its capital expenditures are estimated at US$325 million in 1997 compared to US$374 million in capital and development expenditures in 1996.

The major items include a water treatment facility at Goldstrike, shaft sinking at Rodeo and development of the Pierina Pascua mine, Chief Financial Officer Randall Oliphant said in a speech to shareholders.
"All these costs will be funded entirely from operating cash flow," he said.
Based on Barick's 1997 mining plan production is expected to rise in the second half to produce over three million ouces for the year.
"Earnings will be higher than last year and cash flow will rise to approximately a half billion dollars," Oliphant said.
President John Carrington said Barrick's Meikle mine in the U.S. is exceeding the company's expectations.
"While our 1997 production targets for Meikle is 435,000 ounces, the mine is performing even better than expected," Carrington said in a speech to shareholders.
The mine contains six million high grade ounces and there is room to increase annual production.
Carrington said Meikle will produce gold at a cost of US$125 an ounce.
Carrington also said Barrick's exploration budget for 1997 is about US$100 million -- primarily for work in North and South America and some projects in Asia.
